summary: Alert evaluation failed to trigger for short high-volume spike due to retention compaction gap
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that a short, high-volume traffic spike at 2026-02-17T22:13:00Z did not surface as an alert in Console despite configured threshold (95th percentile token latency > 350ms over 5m). Impact: customer SLO was violated for a paid endpoint; on-call and customer engineers were not notified. Environment: production us-east ingestion cluster. Observed window is immediately after a scheduled retention compaction job.

What happened: LumenOps observed a 4-minute burst of requests generating heavy per-route metrics. Our evaluation job that computes windowed percentiles reported no spike for that 5-minute alert window. The customer provided exporter logs and console query snapshots indicating the raw events exist in the raw event store for the period but rollup data lacked the high-latency buckets.

Why this ticket: We need to determine whether retention compaction job evicted or temporarily aliased buckets used by the alert eval, and implement a fix or mitigation so short bursts are preserved or alert evaluation queries fall back to raw events when compaction boundaries overlap evaluation windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate 4-minute burst of high-latency requests against a single org-scoped route in prod-us-east (token latency ~600ms).
2) Ensure retention compaction run is scheduled at the same minute (the customer's compaction cadence was hourly with boundary at :13).
3) Wait for hourly compaction to complete and then run Console alert eval (95th percentile over the immediately preceding 5m).
4) Compare raw event counts (raw-events API) to aggregated rollup buckets used by alerting service for the same window.
5) If rollup shows no high-latency bucket but raw events do, the compaction path likely removed detail needed by the percentile evaluator.
logs: 2026-02-17T22:12:59Z ingest-processor[writer]: wrote 3,412 events for org: lumenops route: /v1/generate
2026-02-17T22:14:07Z retention-compactor[worker]: merged 1.2M samples, evicted detailed percentile histogram shards: shard_ids=[3421,3422]
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: compaction merged histogram shards and replaced high-resolution histograms with approximated rollup that smoothed out short spikes.
Checked raw-events API: raw-events returns 3,412 events in window with ~7% events reporting >500ms latency.
Checked rollup buckets: corresponding 5m rollup shows 0 events in >400ms bucket; histogram summary shows 95th=128ms.
Confirmed compaction job started within the 5-minute eval window; compaction replaced per-minute histograms with hourly aggregates before alert-eval ran.
Reproducer note: running alert-eval immediately before compaction correctly triggers alert (95th>350ms). Running after compaction returns smoothed result.

2026-02-19 08:01 - LumenOps (Customer): This caused us to miss a critical SLA alert, lost visibility for about 20 minutes. Asking for ETA on fix and whether any credits will be issued.

2026-02-19 12:22 - Ethan Liu (SRE): Mitigation applied: alert-eval now falls back to raw-events query for percentile-based rules when rollup resolution < alert window resolution. Patch deployed to us-east (canary). Monitoring for eval latency impact.

root_cause: Retention compaction job merged high-resolution histogram shards into coarse hourly aggregates while an alert evaluation job for a short 5-minute window ran after compaction but before raw-event fallback was implemented. The coarse aggregate smoothed short spikes, causing percentile-based alert eval to miss the spike.
workaround: Implemented an alert-eval fallback to query raw-events for percentile calculations when the rollup resolution is coarser than the alert window. This is enabled for prod:us-east canary and will be monitored.
resolution: In Progress - mitigation deployed to canary (prod:us-east). Next steps: 1) update compaction policy to keep minute-level histograms for the last 2 hours before compacting to hourly; 2) add unit/integration tests for compaction+alert-eval timing; 3) schedule rolling rollout and customer follow-up.
notes_for_billing: Customer requested credit due to missed SLA. Support manager to coordinate with finance. Temporary goodwill credit proposed for 10% of monthly bill for affected route until fix is rolled out.
